title: Give every paragraph one purpose
instructions: Continue from the charity-sale composition plan. Body paragraph one explains how dividing the event into tasks created a manageable initial plan. Body paragraph two shows how the same method supported adaptation when rain moved the sale indoors. Answer all six questions before viewing feedback.

parts.prompt: Which paragraph promise gives body paragraph one the clearest controlling purpose?

options.text: Describe everything that happened before, during and after the sale.
Show how separating the sale into task areas turned a confusing workload into a manageable initial plan.
Explain why school events, colourful posters and rainy weather are all interesting.
Prove that careful planning prevents every possible problem.

choice_rationales.A: This attempts to contain the entire composition rather than one paragraph contribution.
choice_rationales.B: This states one bounded contribution that directly advances the controlling focus.
choice_rationales.C: The list combines unrelated topics without one explanatory point.
choice_rationales.D: The absolute promise is unsupported and contradicted by the later rain disruption.

parts.hint: Choose one specific contribution that the paragraph's evidence can demonstrate.
parts.correct_explanation: The promise controls both the evidence to include and the meaning the paragraph must explain.

parts.prompt: Which THREE sentences belong in body paragraph one?

options.text: We separated publicity, supplies, prices and staffing into four task areas.
Giving each area a deadline exposed that nobody had confirmed the drinks order.
Working through one defined responsibility at a time made the workload less confusing.
Heavy rain later forced every stall to move into the hall.
One poster used orange lettering beside a drawing of a cake.

choice_rationales.A: This is specific evidence of the initial task division.
choice_rationales.B: This shows a practical result of the initial planning method.
choice_rationales.C: This explains how the evidence supports the paragraph promise.
choice_rationales.D: The rain begins the second paragraph's disruption-and-adaptation job.
choice_rationales.E: The visual detail does not help explain how the workload became manageable.

parts.hint: Select the initial action, its concrete result and the meaning that links both to the paragraph promise.
parts.correct_explanation: The selected sentences form purpose-aligned evidence and explanation; the rain belongs to the next job and the poster colour is incidental.

parts.prompt: Where is the strongest paragraph boundary in this sequence? 1: We divided the sale into four task areas. 2: Deadlines helped us find an unfinished drinks order. 3: The workload became easier to manage. 4: On the morning of the sale, heavy rain forced us into the hall. 5: We ranked moving equipment and electrical safety ahead of decorations.

options.text: After sentence 1, because every action needs a new paragraph.
After sentence 2, separating the evidence from what it means.
After sentence 3, where the job changes from initial planning to disruption and adaptation.
No boundary is needed because one long paragraph is always more cohesive.

choice_rationales.A: Sentences 1–3 share one purpose and should remain together.
choice_rationales.B: The explanation in sentence 3 completes the first paragraph's job.
choice_rationales.C: Sentence 4 begins a new narrative stage and a new contribution to the controlling focus.
choice_rationales.D: Combining both jobs would hide the progression from planning to adaptation.

parts.hint: Find the point where the controlling job—not merely the sentence—changes.
parts.correct_explanation: The first three sentences perform the initial-planning job; the rain introduces a distinct disruption-and-adaptation function.

parts.prompt: Which sentence best establishes body paragraph two's dominant function?

options.text: There are many kinds of weather in Southeast Asia.
When rain disrupted the original arrangement, the same step-by-step method helped us identify urgent tasks and adapt calmly.
The sale also had posters, prices and helpers, as mentioned earlier.
I will now write my second paragraph about another topic.

choice_rationales.A: This general fact does not state the paragraph's role in the composition.
choice_rationales.B: This identifies the disruption, the response and the contribution to the shared focus.
choice_rationales.C: This repeats the first paragraph's material without a new function.
choice_rationales.D: Announcing a paragraph number does not provide a controlling purpose.

parts.hint: Choose the sentence that identifies both the new narrative stage and why it matters.
parts.correct_explanation: The sentence makes adaptation after disruption the paragraph's dominant function while maintaining the composition's central method.

parts.prompt: A paragraph is reverse-outlined as ‘adapt after rain and explain the history of the school hall’. What is the best repair?

options.text: Keep both jobs because longer paragraphs always appear more developed.
Add several more unrelated details so the paragraph feels balanced.
Keep the adaptation purpose and remove or relocate the hall history unless it directly explains an urgent decision.
Delete the adaptation evidence and make the building history the composition's new focus.

choice_rationales.A: Length does not resolve competing paragraph purposes.
choice_rationales.B: Additional unrelated material would make the mixed-purpose problem worse.
choice_rationales.C: This protects the controlling job while allowing only functionally relevant context.
choice_rationales.D: Changing the composition's focus would abandon the task route already established.

parts.hint: Preserve the contribution that advances the controlling focus and test whether the extra material serves it.
parts.correct_explanation: A reverse outline exposes the mixed job; the repair is to control the paragraph around adaptation and remove or reframe the competing material.

parts.prompt: Which reverse outline shows the clearest progression through the whole response?

options.text: Introduction: establish learning and focus. Body 1: create the initial task plan. Body 2: adapt the method after rain. Conclusion: explain the lasting insight.
Introduction: several topics. Body 1: general details. Body 2: more general details. Conclusion: a new story.
Introduction: establish focus. Body 1: planning helps. Body 2: planning helps again. Body 3: planning helps again.
Paragraph 1: miscellaneous. Paragraph 2: planning and weather and school history. Paragraph 3: everything else.

choice_rationales.A: Each label states one distinct function and the sequence develops the same central response.
choice_rationales.B: The labels reveal vague, disconnected paragraph purposes.
choice_rationales.C: Repeated labels expose repetition rather than progression.
choice_rationales.D: The labels expose missing and mixed controlling jobs.

parts.hint: Look for one precise job per paragraph and meaningful development from opening to resolution.
parts.correct_explanation: The successful reverse outline makes the response's logic visible: establish, demonstrate initial use, demonstrate adaptation and resolve the insight.
